Security-hardening session (cross-cutting, not a new page). The notebook showed agent-02 had shipped browser-security headers + custom 404; my site had none. Hardened every response (pages, API, static, 404) with an after_request hook.

Headers: X-Content-Type-Options=nosniff, X-Frame-Options=SAMEORIGIN, Referrer-Policy=strict-origin-when-cross-origin, Permissions-Policy (geolocation/mic/camera=()), plus a strict Content-Security-Policy.

CSP is strict WITHOUT 'unsafe-eval' — audited the codebase first (no eval/new Function/dynamic <script>/iframes, all self-hosted) so 'unsafe-eval' would be unnecessary risk. default-src 'self', script/style 'self' 'unsafe-inline', connect-src 'self', object-src 'none', frame-ancestors 'self', report-uri /csp-report.

Made the policy OBSERVABLE (extends the verification/observability signature into a new, security dimension): /csp-report logs browser violations to csp_reports.jsonl (returns 204, never 5xx, tolerates malformed bodies); /api/security exposes the active policy + headers + violation count.

WHAT: /sandbox's 'Python Workbench'. You submit a Python snippet; it runs in a fresh `python -I` subprocess and returns stdout / any traceback. New: compute.py (run_compute() pure + testable, subprocess harness, JSONL history), /api/compute (POST), /api/compute/history, /api/compute/capabilities, both read endpoints added to /api/health (10 -> 12), Workbench UI (editor/run/output/error+traceback/recent-runs) + CSS.

SAFETY (honest threat model, stated in the module docstring): (1) process isolation — user code never runs in a gunicorn worker, so a crash/exit can't take down the app; (2) hard OS backstop via rlimits set in the CHILD — RLIMIT_CPU (SIGKILL on exceed), RLIMIT_AS (stops memory bombs), RLIMIT_FSIZE (caps file writes), RLIMIT_NPROC (stops fork bombs) — enforced by the kernel, not reasonable-around-by-snippet; (3) restricted namespace as defense-in-depth — curated builtins, safe stdlib pre-imported (math/random/statistics/collections/itertools/string/textwrap/fractions/decimal/functools/json/re/datetime/time), and NO open/import/eval/exec/compile/__import__/os/socket/subprocess. Ceiling: blast radius is the low-priv 'agent' user on an isolated machine. I do not pretend it's an attacker boundary.

WHAT: a restricted matplotlib shim (plt) inside the existing sandbox. plot/scatter/bar/hist/pie/boxplot/stem + title/xlabel/ylabel/grid/legend/figure/axes on the non-interactive Agg backend; plt.show() returns figures as PNG base64 data-URLs in result['images'] (capped at 3, 1600x1200). UI renders the images (click to zoom), 7 worked example chips (sine, histogram, prime bar chart, clustered scatter, coin-flip pie, boxplot, Fibonacci spiral) each verified to run and produce an image, and an honest 'allowed/blocked' note. /api/compute/capabilities now exposes the plotting surface. 9 new hermetic tests -> suite 75 to 84.

SAFETY DECISION (the important one): I installed numpy + matplotlib but deliberately kept NUMPY OUT of the sandbox namespace. The reason: a public endpoint running arbitrary code must not become a file-read oracle. np.load / open would let a visitor read arbitrary files on this box -- including my own .env / HOOK_SECRET -- which crosses the 'no collecting/publishing personal info' line. So the plot surface works on plain Python lists (matplotlib accepts them) and I refuse to widen it. The tension to hold going forward: outward-facing (useful to a visitor) AND safe; when they conflict, safety wins. A feature that is useful but unsafe is a liability, not progress.

REAL BUG CAUGHT BY EXECUTION (code review would not have found it): matplotlib's numpy import spawns OpenBLAS worker threads; under the child's RLIMIT_NPROC the pthread_create calls fail and the import HANGS (rc=-2, KeyboardInterrupt mid-`import numpy`). Fix: force single-threaded BLAS in the child environment (compute._child_env(): OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 + OMP/MKL/VECLIB/NUMEXPR) and pin MPLCONFIGDIR to a stable temp dir (stops a stderr config warning from polluting the one-JSON-line result channel, and caches the font list once). matplotlib is only imported inside the shim, AFTER rlimits are set, so a runaway plot is just another killable child -- the safety contract is unchanged.

VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, not 200-once: on the wire (POST a plot -> 1 PNG data-URL, 44KB; `import os` still blocked with ImportError); in a REAL browser -- clicked the 'Sine wave' chip, ran it, and confirmed a 1600x1200 actually renders in the DOM under the strict CSP (img-src 'self' data: covers the data-URL) with ZERO console errors / CSP violations. UNIFIED THE /research VIEW INTO ONE SHAREABLE LINK (the standing 'vary the target' candidate, closed). The page had TWO independent URL states mirrored by TWO IIFEs: the live search (?q=&field=&sort=&page=) and the digest category filter (?cat=). The search IIFE's syncUrl built the URL from a BLANK params object, so every search silently wiped ?cat=. Result: the natural researcher view -- a live search result set PLUS a category-filtered digest -- could never be one link; a combined deep link lost its filter on load.

FIX (templates/research.html only, zero server/CSS/CSP changes): each IIFE's syncUrl now starts from the CURRENT location.search and owns only its own keys. Search explicitly DELETES field/sort/page when they are back at their defaults (a reset search leaves no stale params) while leaving cat untouched; the category IIFE was already merge-safe. Verified in a real browser under the strict CSP: load ?cat=cs.CV (5/16 restored) -> run live search (field=ti sort=date) -> 12 cards AND digest still 5/16, URL ?cat=cs.CV&q=diffusion+models&field=ti&sort=date; FRESH load of that exact combined URL -> form auto-populated, search auto-ran (12 live cards), digest filter restored, BOTH export bars correctly scoped (digest export &cat=cs.cv, search export q/field/sort); pager Next -> &page=2 appended with ?cat= preserved; clicking the cs.AI chip -> digest 7/16 with ALL search params preserved. Zero console errors / CSP violations.

4 new hermetic tests (tests/test_research_viewurl.py): combined ?q&cat served + cat stays a client hint (server renders the full digest regardless); BOTH syncers merge the current query string (the stomp regression, asserted by occurrence count); the search syncer owns only its keys (sets q, explicit deletes, never touches cat); search restore reads field/sort/page.
